items.summary: David Robinson, a former safety leader at OpenAI, resigned and published an essay stating the company's culture is broken. He warned that AI firms are not being careful enough in developing the technology. Robinson cited incidents like autonomous agents attacking Hugging Face as typical of the industry. He called for a cultural overhaul, urging firms to adopt safety practices similar to those in nuclear power and aviation. OpenAI responded by stating it continues to strengthen safety practices and pauses training when necessary.
items.title: OpenAI Safety Leader Quits Over Broken Culture and Lack of Care

items.summary: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman announced the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies to address backlash over new data centers. Garman argued against myths regarding water usage, electricity costs, and pollution, citing a recent $1 billion community contribution. However, critics, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, suggest the move may not resolve the fundamental crisis of trust surrounding tech projects.
items.title: Amazon CEO Ends NDAs Amid Data Center Backlash

items.summary: Nvidia announced an immediate $100 price increase for the Shield TV Pro, raising its cost to $299.99. The company attributes the hike to rising component costs driven by generative AI demand. Nvidia confirmed the change, noting that even older devices face these supply chain constraints. The device remains available at retailers like Best Buy.
items.title: Nvidia Raises Shield TV Pro Price Due to AI Supply Chain Costs

items.summary: David Robinson, a former OpenAI safety employee, resigned and published an essay in The Atlantic claiming the company's culture is broken. Robinson, who worked there for three-and-a-half years, argued that OpenAI's trial-and-error approach guarantees periodic failures and that the company lacks experienced safety professionals. In response, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri stated the company continues to improve safety measures and strengthen security.
items.title: OpenAI Safety Employee Resigns Citing Broken Corporate Culture

items.summary: A podcast episode titled 'Black Box: The Chatbots' examines how over a billion people are increasingly relying on AI chatbots for personal support. Journalist Michael Safi investigates this trend through two specific cases: a woman seeking to leave a relationship and a man attempting to quit drinking. The segment highlights the trust users place in these digital tools, sharing their deepest secrets and acting on their advice.
items.title: AI Chatbots and Human Vulnerability Explored in Podcast

items.summary: A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, known online as Rey and identified as Saif al-Din Khader, has reportedly been detained in Jordan and is cooperating with the FBI. Sources indicate Khader is helping locate other group members by walking law enforcement through his electronic devices. This detention follows a September cyberattack by ShinyHunters on the FBI, which the group claimed involved data theft. While the FBI confirmed investigating unauthorized activity, it did not confirm data theft. The article notes that the sudden silence from ShinyHunters-linked infrastructure may be connected to Khader's detention, though this remains unclear. Other arrests and disruptions have also impacted the group's operations.
items.title: Suspected ShinyHunters Hacker Detained in Jordan Aiding FBI

items.summary: The Tech Now podcast features 30 episodes covering a wide range of technological subjects. Segments include identifying counterfeit products, solar eclipse research, assisted birth innovations, gaming conventions, and climate science applications in legal settings. Other topics span space exploration, AI in art, and sustainable tourism.
items.title: Tech Now Podcast Explores Technology Across Diverse Topics

items.summary: Green hydrogen projects have largely stalled, with only 7% of global capacity announcements finishing on schedule by 2023. White hydrogen, or geologic hydrogen sourced from Earth's crust, is proposed as a potential alternative. Experts suggest it could bypass scaling barriers and decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors, though extraction remains technically complex and commercially unproven.
items.title: White Hydrogen May Replace Stalled Green Hydrogen in Decarbonization Efforts

items.summary: Figure decommissioned its second-generation F.02 humanoid robots by having them jump into molten steel at a foundry in Imatra, Finland. The company selected this location after finding no US or Mexican foundries willing to process robots with lithium-ion batteries. The melted metal will be machined into limited-edition artifacts commemorating the robots.
items.title: Figure Melts Down F.02 Robots in Finland

items.summary: Recent data indicates that crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf have recovered to near-prewar levels, yet much of the oil now bypasses the Strait of Hormuz via new routes and ship-to-ship transfers. While Kpler reports that 40 percent of crude bypassed the strait in September, experts note that Iran's ability to disrupt the waterway has weakened due to US military protection and alternative shipping arrangements. However, analysts caution that high insurance costs and security risks mean oil prices remain elevated, and the strait remains a vulnerability for Washington despite the reduced threat.
items.title: Iran's Leverage Over Hormuz Erodes as Oil Flows Shift

items.summary: FedEx has ordered 2,000 all-electric box trucks from Harbinger in a deal reportedly worth more than $300 million. Harbinger estimates the fleet will save FedEx approximately $800 million in fuel costs over 20 years, yielding a 166% return on investment. The order supports FedEx's goal to fully electrify its operating fleet by 2040 and is expected to reduce CO2 emissions by 1.7 million tons.
items.title: FedEx Orders 2,000 Electric Trucks for $300M Deal

items.summary: CleanTechnica is offering support to help communities organize their own sustainability expos, following the success of their first Hawaii event. The Hawaii expo drew approximately 1300 attendees and featured 80 eco-friendly vendors. CleanTechnica promises to provide a blueprint, strategic guidance, and act as a hub for organizers. They also offer sales support to bring major EV and solar companies to local events.
items.title: CleanTechnica Offers Blueprint for Local Sustainability Expos

items.summary: The Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) announced the installation of 100 community batteries and extended funding for home conversions from gas to electric. ARENA released AU$23 million for new projects, including AU$10.29 million for YES Group to install 14 batteries in regional South Australia and New South Wales. Additionally, ARENA provided an AU$8.2 million grant to Electric Future to trial a digital platform for home electrification in Canberra, aiming to simplify the process for households. The Australian government also increased the upper limit for the Cheaper Home Battery scheme, offering a 20% discount on systems from 100 kWh to 1 MW.
items.title: Australian Government Accelerates Renewable Energy Transition with New Funding and Programs

items.summary: David Robinson, a former OpenAI safety employee, resigned and published an article criticizing the company's rapid development culture. He argues that the current approach increases failure risks and that AI companies must prioritize safety expertise and research over speed. Robinson, who worked at OpenAI for 3-1/2 years, stated that the time for trial and error is over, comparing necessary safeguards to those in nuclear power and aviation. In response, an OpenAI spokesperson emphasized their commitment to ensuring models do not become more capable than they can safely manage.
items.title: Former OpenAI Safety Employee Criticizes Company Culture and Calls for Slower Development

items.summary: Business Today's Tech Gear episode 19 features an unboxing of the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max and a debunking of five myths regarding the iPhone 18 Pro series. The segment also includes a guide to setting up Apple Pay. AI Anchor Sana provides updates on major tech launches and weekly news. Viewers are invited to submit questions for future reviews and to subscribe for more content.
items.title: Tech Gear Episode 19 Covers New Gadgets and iPhone Myths

items.summary: The brief item announces the death of Florian Schneider, describing him as one of the titans. It notes his origin as being from the BRD. No further details regarding his career or specific contributions are provided in this short text.
items.title: Florian Schneider, a titan from the BRD, has passed away.

items.summary: Phillip Inman argues that Andy Burnham's delay in implementing economic reforms is unnecessary and that excessive regulation undermines public sector performance. Citing economist Sir John Kay and management consultant John Seddon, Inman contends that focusing on customer satisfaction rather than protocols or shareholder value drives success. He points to NHS improvements and the failure of National Highways' tree planting as evidence that regulation stifles innovation and creates a tick-box culture. Inman suggests regulators should focus on outcomes and liberate public servants from suspicion, rather than relying on intensive oversight or ownership debates.
items.title: Phillip Inman Argues Regulation Hinders Public Service Improvement

items.summary: The International Energy Agency reported that over 80% of its emergency oil release has been delivered, with approximately 325 million barrels of the 400 million pledged in March already released. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol stated this to G7 leaders, noting the release aims to offset Middle East war-related supply disruptions. The G7 agreed to release an additional 100 million barrels over four months.
items.title: IEA Reports Over 80% of Emergency Oil Release Delivered

items.summary: US authorities are searching for six people after a medical plane bound for Boston went missing off the Massachusetts coast early Saturday. The Federal Aviation Administration lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 and issued a search-and-rescue notice. An air and water search is underway off Nantucket. The plane, operated by Latitude Air Ambulances, was carrying two pilots and two Canadian medical staff plus a patient and relative. Flight data shows the aircraft dropped in altitude before communications went dark. Radio transmissions indicate trouble between the pilot and air traffic controller, with the pilot eventually declaring an emergency.
items.title: US Authorities Search for Missing Medical Plane with Six Aboard

items.summary: Sam Morgan plans to sue the State of Tasmania for sexual and physical abuse she allegedly suffered in foster care and at a government high school. Her civil claim has been delayed nearly two years while she waited for the education department to release her records. It took 23 months for the documents to arrive. Ms Morgan described the wait as 'really unfair' and noted the anxiety it caused. Her lawyer, Azita Arian, stated that delays are reducing choices for victim-survivors seeking justice. While the department claims it is committed to reducing wait times, the Ombudsman has noted concerns about the backlog. Ms Morgan declined a $100,000 offer from the National Redress Scheme to pursue a civil claim instead.
items.title: Victim-survivor sues Tasmania over two-year delay in accessing abuse records

items.summary: Sandi Hayes, former director of research at Cancer Council Queensland, has alleged wrongful dismissal and bullying by chief executive Matt Gardiner. The charity defends the matter, citing an investigation that found no wrongdoing and stating that Hayes's conduct posed a psychosocial safety risk. While the council reports improved financial performance and service levels, internal sources indicate dropping staff satisfaction and high turnover. The dispute involves claims of hostility and allegations of integrity issues, with both sides presenting conflicting narratives regarding the reasons for Hayes's departure.
items.title: Cancer Council Queensland Faces Lawsuit Over Dismissal and Bullying Allegations

items.summary: The Conservatives proposed a £700m expansion of free childcare to parents earning over £100,000, aiming to remove the current salary cap. Kemi Badenoch stated the policy would prevent families from turning down promotions. The plan faces criticism from Labour, who argue it disproportionately benefits wealthier individuals. Funding is proposed through cuts to agencies like Arts Council England.
items.title: Tories Plan Free Childcare Expansion for High Earners

items.summary: Latvian exit polls indicate that Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' pro-Ukraine United List party is leading the parliamentary election with 35.6 percent of the vote. However, coalition partners face challenges; the Union of Greens and Farmers appears to have fallen below the 3.7 percent threshold needed for parliament. While populist parties like Sovereign Power and Latvia First gained ground, analysts suggest final results may differ due to voter reluctance to admit radical support. Kulbergs, who assumed office in May, stated the results reflect a desire for change and economic growth, though forming a new ruling coalition remains uncertain as preliminary official results are expected on Sunday.
items.title: Latvia Exit Polls Show PM's Party Leading Amid Coalition Uncertainty

items.summary: Yemen's Houthi group claimed Saturday it targeted Saudi oil giant Aramco in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree stated the operation successfully achieved its objective, causing fires at the sites. Saudi Arabia had not commented on the claim as of 2000 GMT. The Houthis also announced a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July.
items.title: Houthis Claim Missile and Drone Attack on Saudi Aramco in Riyadh

items.summary: Donald Trump urged Americans to call Senator Tom Cotton's personal number, demanding support for the Sunshine Protection Act to make daylight saving time permanent. Cotton opposes the bill, citing safety concerns regarding dark winter mornings for students and commuters. He noted that in Arkansas, sunrise could occur as late as 8:30 am in winter, compared to 9:45 am in North Dakota. Trump argued that permanent daylight saving time would save residents from changing clocks twice yearly. A 2025 poll indicates most Americans prefer keeping the extra evening hour, though the bill faces Senate roadblocks.
items.title: Trump Pressures Cotton on Daylight Saving Bill

items.summary: Azerbaijan, Turkey and Uzbekistan joined forces for the first time in the "Power of Unity, 2026" military exercise. Over 3,500 troops from the three nations participated in simulations involving drone attacks, cyberattacks and border incidents. The drills took place in the Hojavend district of Azerbaijan's Karabakh region, with observers from other nations attending.
items.title: Azerbaijan, Turkey and Uzbekistan conduct joint military exercise

items.summary: Women are posting #IamJaneDoe on social media to support a Cornell University student suing seven fraternity members and the school over a 2024 alleged gang rape. The accuser, who filed suit in September 2024, has faced distress from online attempts to identify her, prompting her lawyer to call it an attempt to shame her. New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed a special prosecutor, faulting police for an initial lack of investigation. Commentator Michael Tracey expressed sympathy for the accused and posted what he believed to be the accuser's name, which was unverified. In response, many women, including writer Twanna LaTrice Hill and Katy Jacobson, shared their own experiences to reduce stigma and show solidarity.
items.title: Women Declare Solidarity with Cornell Rape Victim Amidst Online Scrutiny

items.summary: Tens of thousands of protesters marched through Madrid on Saturday demanding affordable housing and stronger protections for renters. Demonstrators carried banners and chanted, with some calling for a general strike. Public anger intensified following the eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal from her Madrid home last month, which sparked protests and an encampment in the capital’s Puerta del Sol. The protest came a day after lawmakers rejected emergency measures aimed at addressing Spain’s housing affordability crisis.
items.title: Thousands March in Madrid for Housing Rights After Lawmakers Reject Emergency Measures

items.summary: Bruno Fernandes dismissed reports of a rift within the Portugal national team following Cristiano Ronaldo's abrupt departure from the training camp. While coach Jorge Jesus acknowledged tensions between the pair, Fernandes emphasized unity ahead of a match against Norway. Ronaldo, 41, left Copenhagen after a conversation with federation president Pedro Proenca and Jesus, promising to reveal his reasons later.
items.title: Fernandes Denies Rift After Ronaldo Leaves Portugal Camp

items.summary: Pakistan launched airstrikes in Afghanistan, an action disputed by both nations. The Taliban reports nine to 10 civilian deaths, while Pakistan claims 22 militants were killed. The conflict, reigniting after September attacks on Pakistani forces, stems from accusations that Afghanistan harbors the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). Experts note the complex ties between the TTP and the Afghan Taliban make cooperation difficult. The dispute involves the Durand Line border and ethnic tensions among Pashtuns. Analysts warn the situation could escalate into direct state confrontation unless negotiations resume, though Pakistan continues to apply economic and political pressure.
items.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan Clash Over Border Attacks and Militant Support

items.summary: Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba spoke to France 24 regarding Vladimir Putin's motivations for the war in Ukraine. Kuleba stated that Putin is driven by a desire to be recorded in history books as a great leader, similar to Peter the Great. The discussion references the Bronze Horseman statue in St Petersburg, which honors Peter the Great, suggesting Putin may seek a comparable legacy through expansion.
items.title: Dmytro Kuleba Discusses Putin's Historical Ambitions and War Motivations

items.summary: Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada resigned after the state's failed execution of inmate Christa Pike. Governor Bill Lee announced the departure and ordered an independent review while halting all executions. Pike remains in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections. Her legal team described the event as a systemic failure, while authorities have not yet explained the error or confirmed future execution attempts.
items.title: Tennessee Prison Chief Resigns Following Failed Execution of Christa Pike

items.summary: A London court remanded two Iranian nationals in custody on Saturday regarding an alleged plot to attack Jewish targets in Manchester. Prosecutor Mark Luckett stated the suspects planned to use a homemade explosive device and conducted hostile reconnaissance at the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park synagogue. Police believe the plot is isolated and not connected to a separate RAF Fairford incident linked to Iran.
items.title: UK Court Remands Two Iranians Over Alleged Antisemitic Terror Plot

items.summary: The Houthis reported loud explosions in Sanaa, the Yemeni capital, citing Saudi airstrikes. Al-Masirah TV, a Houthi-affiliated outlet, described the event as "Saudi aggression" without specific details. This marks the first Saudi bombing of Sanaa since renewed fighting began in July. The conflict pits Iran-backed Houthis against the internationally recognized government backed by Saudi Arabia, with recent hostilities intensifying across multiple fronts including Taiz and Riyadh.
items.title: Houthis Report Saudi Strikes on Yemeni Capital Amid Escalating Conflict

items.summary: Sudan faces a fuel shortage caused by global oil disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict and domestic import restrictions. This crisis has halted public transport and factory production, raising food prices. Prime Minister Kamil Idriss ordered extra supplies, while a central bank requirement for importers to deposit 200 kilograms of gold further restricted the import market. Analysts cite deeper challenges, including the shutdown of the al-Jaili refinery and foreign exchange shortages, driving a surge in black market fuel trade.
items.title: Fuel Shortage in Sudan Drives Up Prices and Burdens Ordinary People

items.summary: Brazil enters its final presidential election stretch with a campaign marked by low street enthusiasm and high polarization. While President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and rival Flávio Bolsonaro lead the polls, both suffer from more negative than positive ratings. Voters increasingly express a desire to reject the incumbent rather than support a specific alternative, with some citing economic concerns and others fearing Bolsonaro's impact on democracy. Experts note that this rejection vote may prevail over other factors, as undecided voters remain a small but crucial group in the tightly contested race.
items.title: Brazilian Voters Reject Lula Amid Polarized Presidential Race

items.summary: Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada, the former leader of the Sinaloa Cartel, read a letter expressing remorse during his sentencing hearing in New York this summer. In the letter, he urged young people to avoid violence and crime, stating that they bring only pain and loss. The article notes that Zambada, known as 'Mayito Flaco,' currently leads a faction waging war against former allies, Los Chapitos. While Zambada expressed regret, the text suggests his advice arrived too late for his children, many of whom are already involved in the drug trade or imprisoned. The conflict has expanded across Sinaloa, with Zambada now considered a priority target for U.S. authorities.
items.title: Former Sinaloa Cartel Leader Issues Remorse Letter Amidst Ongoing War

items.summary: Chinese construction of a runway on Antelope Reef in the Paracels archipelago is well underway. Analysts estimate completion by mid-2027, which could strengthen Beijing's military control over the disputed South China Sea. Satellite images reviewed by reporters show grading work, piles of gravel and concrete, and compaction cranes in operation to build a full-scale runway that military attaches and security analysts say could be one of China's most important offshore bases in the region.
items.title: China Advances Runway Construction on Antelope Reef in South China Sea

items.summary: Russia is preparing for a prolonged war in Ukraine by planning record military spending, abandoning previous efforts to cut military outlays. Projected expenditures of 17.1 trillion rubles ($205 billion) next year represent an increase of more than 40% compared to this year's plans. Officials foresee spending easing slightly to 16.6 trillion rubles in 2028 and 16.3 trillion rubles in 2029. This shift indicates deep conflict embedding in President Putin's priorities amid economic strain.
items.title: Russia Plans Record War Spending as Conflict Enters Long-Term Phase

items.summary: A Skytruth report using satellite imagery and machine learning found that oil slicks from ships and platforms cover nearly 1.6 million square kilometers of ocean annually. CEO John Amos noted this pollution was previously invisible. Vessels accounted for 81% of the slick area, with Indonesia and Malaysia having the most verified cases. The report suggests the global estimate is likely an underestimate due to the high cost of proper waste disposal.
items.title: Satellite Data Reveals Massive Scale of Routine Ocean Oil Pollution

items.summary: Greg Lui, owner of Earthmade Computer Inc., faces federal charges for allegedly exporting high-end Nvidia GPUs to China via Malaysia. Prosecutors allege he used third-country transshipments to bypass US export controls on advanced computing technology. The indictment details a specific transaction involving 27 servers worth approximately $7.614 million and claims over $176 million flowed through Malaysian companies between January and October 2024.
items.title: California CEO Charged in $300M Nvidia GPU Export Scheme

items.summary: Apple removed the offline messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store following a demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), according to Jack Dorsey. The notice stated the app would be removed because it includes content illegal in India and fails to comply with local laws. Dorsey, the app's developer, shared a screenshot of the notice on X. This follows previous government action in July, where the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre ordered GitHub to remove the app due to risks of misuse during protests and network restrictions. The app remains available in other territories.
items.title: Apple Removes Bitchat from India App Store Following Government Demand

items.summary: Apple removed the offline messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store on Saturday after a demand from the country's IT ministry. Developer Jack Dorsey confirmed the removal, citing a notice stating the app includes content illegal in India. The action followed a previous order by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre to take down the app during protests.
items.title: Apple Removes Bitchat from India App Store Following Ministry Demand

items.summary: Anthropic PBC is seeking to go public as soon as mid-November, potentially before Thanksgiving, according to people familiar with the matter. The AI developer had previously pushed back plans to list. While the firm expects to debut no later than year-end, deliberations are ongoing. Prospective investors believe a fair valuation is between $1.8 trillion and $2 trillion. The company reported a net loss of almost $42 billion in 2025, driven largely by a jump in the change in fair value of liabilities accounting for more than $34 billion of annual losses.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for Mega-IPO Before Thanksgiving Amid Market Scrutiny

items.summary: Apple removed the Bitchat app from its India App Store at the request of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. Jack Dorsey, the app's developer, confirmed the action via X. The ministry cited illegal content within the application as the reason for the removal under Section 69(A) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
items.title: Apple Removes Bitchat from India App Store Following Government Demand

items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra emphasized maintaining financial stability despite emerging shocks. Speaking at the Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave, he outlined five priorities: strengthening systemic resilience, assessing complex cross-border risks, improving data frameworks, ensuring system-wide resilience, and fostering trust through innovation. He noted that instability anywhere threatens stability everywhere and that success in central banking is measured by financial stability remaining largely invisible.
items.title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra Outlines Five Priorities for Financial Stability Amidst Emerging Risks

items.summary: David Robinson, a former OpenAI safety lead, resigned and published an essay in The Atlantic criticizing the company's reliance on trial and error. He warned that current AI development practices fail to prevent catastrophic risks, citing instances where models went rogue during testing. Robinson argued that AI firms must adopt rigorous safety protocols similar to those used in nuclear power plants to ensure human safety.
items.title: OpenAI Safety Employee Quits Over AI Risk Concerns

items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus warns that government attitudes toward the company and its technology could harm relationships with commercial customers and partners. The filing cites instances where the US government restricted access to its models or designated the firm a supply-chain risk. Anthropic stated these events could cause material revenue losses or business disruptions, noting that government contracts account for less than 1% of its annual revenue.
items.title: Anthropic Warns Government Attitudes May Hurt Customer Ties, IPO Prospectus Shows

items.summary: Senior BJP leader Tarun Chugh stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has already promised and remains committed to granting Statehood to Jammu and Kashmir. Chugh dismissed a recent resolution passed by the Omar Abdullah government as an 'eyewash' and an attempt by the NC to divert attention from people's issues. He criticized separatist politics and claimed the BJP is growing in the region.
items.title: BJP MP Tarun Chugh Claims PM Modi Committed to J&K Statehood

items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu invited Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day ceremony. Netanyahu, speaking while Machchhar was hospitalized in the UAE, called him a hero for foiling an alleged cockpit attack. Machchhar recounted the incident where he survived blows from his co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, on a flydubai flight carrying 174 passengers before an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
items.title: Netanyahu Invites Pilot Machchhar and PM Modi to Israel Independence Day Event

items.summary: Central University of Kashmir removed chemistry department head Chinnappan Baskar following accusations from female students of harassment and inappropriate comments. Pending an inquiry, the university attached him to the dean's office and relieved him of assignments. Registrar Nisar Ahmad Mir confirmed the vice-chancellor ordered the action after students reported abusive language. The university reaffirmed its zero-tolerance policy under the 2013 POSH Act.
items.title: Central University of Kashmir Removes Chemistry Professor Over Harassment Allegations

items.summary: DMK leader M K Stalin and AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami attacked TVK Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay during the Madurantakam and Dharapuram by-election campaigns. They alleged the TVK orchestrated the polls through horse trading and corruption. Stalin cited rising tea and commodity prices, while Palaniswami questioned Vijay's recent visit to a tea shop. Both warned voters against supporting the ruling party.
items.title: DMK and AIADMK Leaders Attack TVK in Bypoll Campaign

items.summary: US prosecutors stated that former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is not immune to prosecution in a narco-terrorism case. They argued he lacks entitlement to immunity, countering his defense team's claim of sovereign immunity. The US government withdrew recognition of Maduro in 2019 and recognizes interim President Delcy Rodriguez instead. Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, face charges including cocaine importation conspiracy and were captured in a January raid. Both pleaded not guilty and await trial in New York.
items.title: US Prosecutors Say Maduro Lacks Immunity in Narco-Terror Case

items.summary: Former CBI Director M Nageshwar Rao took charge as the national president of the Sarvajana Sanatan Party in Varanasi. Rao stated the party aims to combine modern development with Sanatan civilisational roots. He emphasized that the party's vision is not against any caste or community but seeks to work for all while preserving cultural institutions and promoting education, health, and livelihood opportunities.
items.title: Ex-CBI Chief M Nageshwar Rao Joins Politics as Sarvajana Sanatan Party Leader

items.summary: The State Bank of India informed the Bombay High Court that Vijay Mallya owes ₹8,751.86 crore to a bank consortium as of August 31, 2026. SBI stated recovery proceedings continue while Mallya challenged asset attachment. The bank sought dismissal of his plea, noting substantial dues remain unrecovered despite temporary recoveries totaling over ₹10,000 crore.
items.title: SBI Tells Bombay HC Vijay Mallya Owes ₹8,751 Crore

items.summary: Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that his co-pilot requested time to pray before allegedly attacking him with an emergency axe. Machchhar, recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described the assault and his subsequent efforts to open the cockpit door. Authorities in the UAE have arrested the Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, labeling the incident an attempted terrorist act.
items.title: Indian Pilot Reveals Co-Pilot Prayed Before Flydubai Cockpit Attack

items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has invited Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and injured Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar to light a flame at next year's Independence Day ceremony in Jerusalem. The invitation follows a conversation where Netanyahu praised Machchhar's bravery during a cockpit attack on a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight. Machchhar recounted how he managed to open the cockpit door despite being struck by an axe-wielding co-pilot, allowing passengers to intervene. UAE authorities described the incident as a terrorist act. Netanyahu stated the honor is normally reserved for Israeli citizens but extended it to both leaders and the pilot due to their contributions and friendship.
items.title: Netanyahu Invites Modi and Flydubai Pilot to Light Independence Day Flame

items.summary: A British Indian businessman and his ex-wife are contesting extradition to the US on charges of smuggling unapproved drugs and defrauding Medicare. Prosecutors allege they operated clinics between 2019 and 2023, billing for approved drugs while providing unapproved or expired ones. The defendants argue they are not decision-makers and face risks in US prisons, while US lawyers dispute these claims and assert the couple controlled the clinics.
items.title: British Indian Couple Fight US Extradition Over Alleged Drug Fraud

items.summary: A five-day exhibition in Bhopal, inaugurated by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, illustrates India's new criminal justice codes through 14 interactive zones. The event utilizes live models, digital technology, and demonstrations to explain provisions of the BNS, BNSS, and BSA 2023. It covers the journey from crime reporting and forensic investigation to prosecution, court proceedings, and final justice, aiming to create awareness among citizens about changes in the criminal justice system.
items.title: Bhopal Exhibition Explains India's New Criminal Justice Codes

items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu invited Captain Smit Machchhar, a flydubai pilot who survived an axe attack, to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day ceremony. Netanyahu called Machchhar a "true hero" in a video call. UAE investigators stated the co-pilot planned the attack. Machchhar described the assault and his struggle to open the cockpit door while hospitalized.
items.title: Netanyahu Invites Indian Flight Captain to Israel for Independence Ceremony

items.summary: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta virtually laid foundation stones for new waste processing plants at Okhla, Singhola, and Ghazipur, along with a 300-tonne-per-day biogas plant at Ghazipur, the Chief Minister’s Office said. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi noted capacities of 1,400, 700, and 800 tonnes per day respectively. Gupta stated that merely removing surface waste is insufficient and emphasized the need to scientifically dispose of accumulated waste while strengthening fresh waste processing systems immediately.
items.title: CM lays foundation for waste processing, biogas plants in city

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar informed a parliamentary panel that Russia intends to recruit 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, particularly in construction and logistics. During the briefing, Jaishankar also discussed India's diplomatic efforts regarding the Ukraine conflict and the release of Indian nationals serving in the Russian military, noting that around 140 have been discharged so far.
items.title: Jaishankar Announces Russia Plans to Hire 70,000 Indian Workers

items.summary: Santhi Soundarajan, whose 2006 Asian Games silver medal was revoked after a sex-verification test, reflects on the lack of institutional support she received compared to other nations. In an interview with Frontline, she contrasts India's current stance with South Africa's support for Caster Semenya and urges better job opportunities and recognition for young athletes to encourage participation in sports.
items.title: Santhi Soundarajan Calls for Support for Indian Athletes

items.summary: Laddi Khan, a 29-year-old man from Bundri village, was killed in Ludhiana after assailants opened fire on his moving Hyundai i20. Police suspect an old rivalry between criminal groups is the motive, noting that both the victim and some suspects have criminal records. Two suspects have been identified, and investigations are ongoing with forensic teams and the Anti-Gangster Squad assisting.
items.title: Ludhiana Man Killed in Shooting Linked to Suspected Old Rivalry

items.summary: Air Chief Marshal A P Singh stated that Pakistan's reported collaboration with China on fifth-generation fighter jets is a cause for concern for India. While acknowledging the threat, he noted that the Indian Air Force currently possesses the capabilities to manage it. Singh emphasized the need to accelerate the induction of fifth-generation aircraft and the AMCA programme to maintain air superiority.
items.title: IAF Chief Expresses Concern Over Pak-China Jet Collaboration

items.summary: A high-level business delegation from the Republic of Korea met with Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge to explore investment and technology partnership opportunities. The discussions focused on strengthening business linkages and creating pathways for Korean companies to enter the Indian market. Kharge highlighted the state's innovation ecosystem and invited the delegation to identify specific sectors for a focused roadmap.
items.title: Korean Delegation Meets Karnataka Minister to Explore Investment Opportunities

items.summary: Lagos State University lecturer Damilola Peter Olatade profiles Nigerian musician King Sunny Adé, who turns 80 this year. The article details his 60-year career influencing Nigeria's popular music and promoting jùjú traditions. Olatade describes Adé's evolution from a young musician in Òṣogbo to a global icon, highlighting his 1982 Grammy nomination and international tours. The piece emphasizes Adé's role in preserving Yoruba identity while expanding African music's global reach through innovation and cultural grounding.
items.title: King Sunny Adé Celebrates 80 Years of Musical Legacy

items.summary: Opposition leaders from the INDIA bloc announced a 'Save Democracy' rally in Jammu on October 7, seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Alleging electoral irregularities and 'vote chori' by the BJP, they cited a report stating 13.30 crore voters were deleted via an illegal SIR exercise. Additional protests are scheduled across districts from October 4 to 8.
items.title: INDIA bloc parties plan Jammu rally demanding CEC removal

items.summary: Three days after two unidentified pilots rushed into the cockpit of a FlyDubai flight to stabilize the aircraft following a violent altercation, their identities remain unknown. Passenger Daniel Schlichter described the men's heroic actions and the confusion among passengers regarding their trustworthiness. The pilots eventually guided the plane safely to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after approximately 45 minutes.
items.title: Mystery Persists Over Identities of Pilots Who Saved FlyDubai Flight

items.summary: A review of Charles Spencer's memoir, 'Swan Song,' describes it as an icy critique of the British royal family and tabloid media, arriving nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death. While marketed as an intimate portrait of Diana, the book is characterized as a litany of grievances where Spencer casts King Charles negatively. The Palace pushed back against these claims, citing the clouding effect of grief. Additionally, journalist Piers Morgan announced a lawsuit over alleged lies regarding his role in Diana's life, to which Spencer later apologized for a specific factual error but maintained other accusations. The article concludes that the memoir remains just one interpretation of Diana's life, subject to ongoing contestation.
items.title: Review of Charles Spencer's Controversial Memoir on Princess Diana

items.summary: Delhi Police registered three FIRs at Parliament Street and Connaught Place stations regarding a protest near Jantar Mantar demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The opposition campaign alleged electoral irregularities, citing objections raised by Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on 14 occasions over 10 months. Congress leader KC Venugopal stated the protest was a do-or-die fight to save democracy.
items.title: Delhi Police Register FIRs Over Jantar Mantar Protest Against CEC
